blocks.content: Movement of magma and tectonic stress often generate earthquakes near volcanic regions. Thus, volcanic belts frequently overlap with seismic belts.

items: Volcanic belts and seismic belts frequently overlap rather than existing in isolation.
Movement of magma and tectonic stress are the primary causes generating earthquakes near volcanic regions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Earthquakes in volcanic regions are generated by magma movement and tectonic stress.
The spatial distribution of volcanic activity closely aligns with seismic activity.
Volcanic belts frequently overlap with seismic belts.
